finalAnswer:
I checked your two-point track (about 13.2 nm, with a 2 nm corridor each side) against the Coast Guard's NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers. The check ran on 8 Oct 2026 at 21:29 UTC, so "tomorrow" is 9 Oct. The check has gaps, listed below, so don't treat it as clear of other restrictions.

## Notices that affect the track

**1. Dredging at Lamberts Point Pier 6, Elizabeth River (MSI #53466)**
- **Status:** it becomes effective on 9 Oct, your transit day, and runs to 4 Jan 2027.
- **Location:** it intersects the track at the Elizabeth River end, right at your destination point of 36.88,-76.33.
- **What's happening:** the notice says mechanical dredging "will commence on or about October 21, 2026". It uses the dredge KOKO V, tugs and scows, and they will monitor VHF 13.
- **What it means for you:** work probably won't start on 9 Oct, but the notice becomes effective that day. Expect possible tugs and scows near Pier 6, and call VHF 13 if you see them.

**2. Dredging at Norfolk International Terminals (MSI #54120)**
- **Status:** active from 22 Sep 2026 to 3 Feb 2027.
- **Location:** about 1.1 nm from the track, near the Elizabeth River end.
- **What's happening:** the dredge CB Harry S is held by 4 anchors marked with lighted ball buoys, with tender tug Kimberly S.
- **What it means for you:** the notice asks vessels to use caution and keep no wake when passing the work area. Scows are towed out to the offshore disposal site (NODS).

**3. Vibracore sampling in Thimble Shoal Channel East (MSI #54261)**
- **Status:** active from 26 Sep to 25 Oct 2026, with sampling on 13–24 Oct, daily 0600–1800. The notice also lists 27–29 Sep. Operations on 9 Oct are not stated.
- **Location:** about 1.3 nm from the track, near your starting point.
- **What's happening:** the M/V BRANDY STATION is restricted in her ability to maneuver while sampling.
- **What it means for you:** the notice asks for caution, reduced speed and a slow bell when passing, and contact on VHF 13 or 16.

**4. Temporary aid change: Elizabeth River Lighted Buoy 29 (relocated for dredging)**
- **Status:** the notice has no effective dates and no text.
- **Location:** about 1.6 nm from the track.
- **What it means for you:** don't rely on the charted position of this buoy.

**5. District 5 marine event permit notice (MSI #45232)**
- This is an administrative notice about the permit application process. It covers a very large area and has no effect on your transit.

## Gaps in the check

- **Safety zones weren't checked.** The Coast Guard lists the safety zone file (safeZoneLine_1) but returns a 404 for it. Zero safety zone matches therefore means nothing here. Hampton Roads has security zones and moving zones around Navy and commercial vessels, so check the Coast Guard Sector Virginia Local Notice to Mariners and the Captain of the Port page.
- **Broadcast Notices to Mariners weren't checked**, and neither were bridge notices, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, Light List data, NOAA charts, NGA NAVAREA warnings, weather or tides.
- **The route is two points joined by a straight line.** I didn't plan it around land or channels, so a real route through Thimble Shoal and Hampton Roads may pass closer to some of these notices.

Before you go, get the latest Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and listen to VHF broadcasts. This is official-notice information, not navigational advice.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

finalAnswer:
I found 12 active USCG notices within 2 nm of the route, but the check is incomplete. The USCG safety-zone dataset (`safeZoneLine_1`) is listed by NAVCEN but returned a 404, so any safety zones near the route were not checked. The route is about 3.9 nm long, and the data was checked on 2026-10-08.

**Hazard to navigation (1)**
- **Bass River shoaling (MSI 296):** Severe shoaling is reported between Bass River Channel Buoys 2 and 9, with a much narrower channel. It is about 0.89 nm from the route, near the end point. It runs from 2024-09-12 to 2039-12-21.

**Marine construction (3)**
The same contractor (AGM Marine Contractors) is removing three USCG daybeacons. The work uses the dredge PRONCKAI, deck barge THING and tug SITKA. It runs about 6 am to 8 pm daily, from roughly Sep 28 to Nov 15, 2026. Listen on VHF 13 and 16, with 68 as the working channel.
- **Abbott Rock Daybeacon (MSI 54061):** about 0.23 nm from the route, at 42°31.8'N 070°51.7'W.
- **Lobster Rock Daybeacon (MSI 54065):** about 0.53 nm from the route, at 42°32.3'N 070°52.9'W.
- **Bowditch Ledge Daybeacon (MSI 54064):** about 1.59 nm from the route, at 42°32.4'N 070°48.7'W.

**Marine events (8)**
Seven of these are regattas in Marblehead Harbor and Salem Sound (chart 13275). Six of the seven have areas that the route passes through directly. All were hosted by the Eastern Yacht Club except the frostbiting series, which is run by the Boston Yacht Club.
- **Etchells New England Championships (MSI 37107):** Oct 8–11, 11 am–4 pm, about 30 boats.
- **Nessa Keelboat High School Championships (MSI 36980):** Oct 10, 9 am–4 pm, and Oct 11, 9 am–12 pm, about 12 boats.
- **Pumpkin Pursuit Race 2 (MSI 37099):** Oct 17, 12–4 pm, about 15 boats.
- **Halloween Team Race (MSI 36959):** Oct 24–25, 9 am–4 pm, about 15 boats.
- **Pumpkin Pursuit Race 3 (MSI 37101):** Oct 24, 12–4 pm, about 15 boats.
- **Fall Laser ILCA Series (MSI 36841):** Sundays through Nov 22, 1–3 pm, about 15 boats.
- **BYC Tech Dinghy Frostbiting Series (MSI 52676):** Sundays from Nov 8 through Apr 4, 2027, 12–2 pm. It is about 0.35 nm from the route and does not cross it. The record's validity window starts Oct 8, but the text says Nov 8.
- **Beverly 400 Battle Reenactment (MSI 35689):** Oct 10, 9–11 am, off Independence Park in Beverly Harbor (chart 13276). Two sailing vessels. It crosses the route near the end point.

**Not covered by this check**
- The check did not include Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, or records with no geometry.
- Non-USCG sources such as NOAA charts and NGA NAVAREA warnings were also not checked.
- This is not navigational advice. Check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and listen to VHF before you transit.

finalAnswer:
**Yes, one safety zone is in effect within 10 nm of that position. Whether it's being enforced today (Oct 8, 2026) I couldn't confirm.**

**Glen Island Approach Bridge safety zone, New Rochelle, NY**
- **Distance:** it sits about 0.2 nm from your position. Its corners are around 40°53′19″–23.8″ N, 73°46′52″–59″ W, along the shore at Glen Island.
- **Authority:** Captain of the Port New York, 33 CFR 165.T01-0956 (89 FR 95720, docket USCG-2024-0956).
- **Effective period:** Dec 2, 2024 through 5 p.m. May 27, 2027.
- **Hours:** 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily, but enforced only while bridge rehabilitation work is in progress.
- **Rule:** no vessel or person may enter without COTP permission. Contact Sector New York on VHF-FM 16 or (844) 692-8724.
- **Closure windows:** the rule listed a tentative full-channel closure from 7 a.m. Oct 2 to 5 p.m. Oct 29, 2026, which would cover today. The rule itself said this schedule was only "being considered" and could change. The Coast Guard says it announces enforcement through the Local Notice to Mariners and VHF Channel 16 broadcasts.

**Other zones nearby**
- The recurring fireworks and swim-event safety zones, such as the Orchard Beach, Bronx launch site (about 1 nm away) and Little Neck Bay (about 6 nm away), only apply when enforced for a specific event. I didn't find any enforcement notice for them this week. A 2023 rule reorganized that list, and I didn't check whether the Orchard Beach zone was removed.
- The Wantagh/Zach's Bay and Oyster Bay zones are outside 10 nm.

My search covered the Federal Register and a web search, not the live Local Notice to Mariners or the Coast Guard's Homeport site. Short-notice zones, such as a one-day escort or exercise zone, wouldn't show up in what I checked. Before you go out, check the First District Local Notice to Mariners (navcen.uscg.gov), call Sector New York, or listen to VHF 16.

###### Department of Homeland Security

###### Coast Guard

1.  33 CFR Part 165
2.  \[Docket Number USCG-2024-0956\]
3.  RIN 1625-AA00

# AGENCY:

Coast Guard, DHS.

# ACTION:

Temporary interim rule and request for comments.

# SUMMARY:

The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for certain waters of Long Island Sound in the vicinity of the Glen Island Approach Bridge, New Rochelle, NY, for construction vessels and machinery involved in the rehabilitation project of the bridge. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards associated with the bridge construction between December 2, 2024, through May 27, 2027. When enforced, this regulation prohibits persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless authorized by the Captain of the Port New York or a designated representative.

# DATES:

This rule is effective without notice from December 3, 2024, through 5 p.m. on May 27, 2027. For the purposes of enforcement, actual notice will be used from midnight on December 2, 2024, until December 3, 2024. This rule will only be enforced during periods when construction operations at the bridge are in progress.

Comments and related material must be received by the Coast Guard on or before March 3, 2025.

# ADDRESSES:

To view documents mentioned in this preamble as being available in the docket, go to _[https://www.regulations.gov](https://www.regulations.gov/),_ type USCG-2024-0956 in the search box and click “Search.” Next, in the Document Type column, select “Supporting & Related Material.”

# FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:

If you have questions about this rule, call or email Jeffrey Yunker, Waterways Management Division, U.S. Coast Guard Sector New York; telephone 718-354-4195, email _[Jeffrey.M.Yunker@uscg.mil](mailto:Jeffrey.M.Yunker@uscg.mil)._

# SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

## I. Table of Abbreviations

CFR Code of Federal Regulations

DHS Department of Homeland Security

## II. Background Information and Regulatory History

On August 26, 2024, the Westchester County Department of Public Works and Transportation notified the U.S. Coast Guard of the Glen Island Bridge rehabilitation project and the need for waterway closures on the Long Island Sound. This project will establish a temporary bridge to Glen Island while the current bridge undergoes repairs. The Westchester County and the New Rochelle Harbor Master have provided information to the public and interested stakeholders through an established project page maintained by the county located at _[https://publicworks.westchestergov.com/​glen-island-approach-bridge-rehabilitation](https://publicworks.westchestergov.com/glen-island-approach-bridge-rehabilitation)._ This project page has been updated throughout the project and will be maintained to provide updated information to the public until the bridge rehabilitation project is finished. The contractor Kiewit Infrastructure Company has already conducted public outreach meetings with affected mariners and plans additional meetings to address any concerns with regards to the waterway closures in the future.

The Coast Guard is issuing this temporary rule under the authority in [5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/5/553). This statutory provision authorizes an agency to issue a rule without prior notice and opportunity to comment when the agency for good cause finds that those procedures are “impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.” The Coast Guard finds that good cause exists for not publishing a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) with respect to this rule because prompt action is needed to respond to the potential safety hazards associated with the establishment of a temporary bridge and bridge repairs to the existing Glen Island Bridge. Publishing an NPRM would be impracticable and contrary to public interest because a safety zone must be established by December 2, 2024, to ensure that the construction project is not delayed. Any delay in the project would adversely impact vehicle users and mariners in the future.

Also, under [5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3)](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/5/553), the Coast Guard finds that good cause exists for making this rule effective less than 30 days after publication in the **Federal Register** . Delaying the effective date of this rule would be impracticable because prompt action is needed to respond to the potential safety hazards associated with the establishment of a ( printed page 95721) temporary bridge and the construction associated with the rehabilitation of the existing Glen Island Bridge.

Although this regulation is published as an interim rule without prior notice, public comment is nevertheless desirable to ensure that the regulation is both workable and reasonable. Accordingly, persons wishing to comment may do so by submitting written comments as set out under **ADDRESSES** in this preamble. Commenters should include their names and addresses, identify the docket number for the regulation, and give reasons for their comments. If the Coast Guard determines that changes to the temporary interim rule are necessary, we will publish a temporary final rule or other appropriate document.

## III. Legal Authority and Need for Rule

The Coast Guard is issuing this rule under authority in [46 U.S.C. 70034](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/46/70034). The Captain of the Port New York (COTP) has determined that potential safety hazards associated with the establishment of a temporary bridge and bridge repairs to the existing Glen Island Bridge from December 2, 2024, through May 27, 2027, constitutes a safety concern for anyone near the waters of Glen Island and in the vicinity of bridge repair vessels and machinery. This rule is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment in the navigable waters within the safety zone while the bridge is being repaired.

## IV. Discussion of the Rule

This rule establishes a safety zone from 7 a.m. until 5 p.m. each day starting on midnight December 2, 2024, through May 27, 2027. The safety zone will only be enforced during periods when construction operations at the Glen Island Bridge rehabilitation project are in progres

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

**Result:** 8 active USCG notices fall within 5 nm of 36.95 N 76.33 W. The check ran on 2026‑10‑09 at about 12:10 UTC. The coverage is incomplete, so this is not a full list (see the caveats below).

**Safety zones (HRBT Expansion Project)**

COTP Sector Virginia keeps six safety zones in place to protect the Hampton Roads Bridge‑Tunnel (HRBT) expansion. The rule is 33 CFR 165.T05‑1069 and the zones are enforceable until 20 Dec 2030, or earlier if the COTP decides they are no longer needed. Three of the six are within 5 nm:

| MSI # | Location | Distance from point | Valid |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34480 | Willoughby Bay | 1.8 nm | 2025‑12‑25 to 2030‑12‑20 |
| 34479 | James River | 3.0 nm | 2025‑12‑25 to 2030‑12‑20 |
| 34481 | James River | 3.0 nm | 2025‑12‑25 to 2030‑12‑20 |

**Marine construction**

| MSI # | Location | Distance from point | Valid | Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 54120 | Norfolk International Terminals (Elizabeth River) | 1.9 nm | 2026‑09‑22 to 2027‑02‑03 | Dredge *CB Harry S* works the North Container Terminal. It is held by 4 anchors marked with lighted ball buoys and has a tender tug. Scows are towed to NODS. Vessels should use caution and no wake. |
| 53466 | Lambert's Point Pier 6 (Elizabeth River) | 4.2 nm | 2026‑10‑09 to 2027‑01‑04 | Dredge *KOKO V* with tugs and scows. Work starts on or about 21 Oct. Crews monitor VHF 13. |
| 32591 | Newport News Creek, 36°58'16"N 76°24'57"W | 4.3 nm | 2025‑11‑21 to 2027‑03‑31 | Pier demolition and reconstruction with crane barges, 07:00–15:30 on weekdays. Use no wake within 500 ft. Crews monitor VHF 13 and 16. |
| 53462 | Kinder Morgan Bulk Terminals (Newport News, James River) | 4.8 nm | 2026‑09‑24 to 2027‑01‑04 | *KOKO V* dredging, with work starting on or about 1 Oct. Crews monitor VHF 13. |

**Marine event (administrative)**

MSI 45232 covers all of District 5 through 30 Nov 2026. It announces the new online Marine Event Permit application process. Sponsors should apply to the Captain of the Port at least 135 days before an event. It does not restrict navigation.

**Caveats**
- **Missing safety‑zone layer:** The safety‑zone line dataset (`safeZoneLine_1`) returned HTTP 404 from NAVCEN. Any safety zones published only as lines were not checked, so the three safety zones above may not be all of them.
- **Not checked:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners, NGA NAVAREA IV warnings, bridge notices, aids‑to‑navigation discrepancies, Light List data, and NOAA chart updates.
- **Results by category:** No hazards to navigation, naval activity, space operations, temporary aids‑to‑navigation changes, TESS advisories or MSIBs were found in the layers that were checked.
- **Use for planning only:** This is not navigational advice. Before transiting, check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners (navcen.uscg.gov/msi), listen to Sector Virginia VHF broadcasts, and monitor VHF 13 and 16.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

**Yes. One USCG space operations hazard area is in the notice window and about 24.7 nm from your position, so it only just falls inside your 25 nm radius.** The check ran on 2026-10-09 at about 12:12 UTC against the USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers.

**Notice 54068: Hazardous Warning Area (Commercial), Sector San Diego / EEZ, District 11**
- **Operation:** SpaceX Starlink g15-25 launch.
- **Notice window:** 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-18 UTC. This is the notice's validity period. The actual hazard times are listed in the next section.
- **Distance:** The area is 24.7 nm from 33.80N, 119.30W. Your point is not inside it.
- **Location:** A long, narrow area running from the Vandenberg coast (about 34.67N, 120.6W) southeast to about 28.2N, 117.3W. It is split into Hazard Areas A and B, and the part nearest you is the northern end.

**Hazard times (UTC), each window running about 4 hours:**
- **Primary:** 10 Oct 2300Z to 11 Oct 0325Z (Area A) and 0343Z (Area B).
- **Backup days:** The same window repeats daily from 11 Oct 2300Z through 16 Oct 2300Z, ending 17 Oct.
- **Local time:** The primary window is the afternoon and evening of 10 Oct in California, about 4:00 pm to 8:30 pm PDT.

The hazard area itself is only in force during those windows. The notice is current but the hazard is not yet in effect.

**Caveats**
- The area sits right at the edge of your radius, so small position or distance differences matter.
- The data tool did not check Broadcast Notices to Mariners (BNM), NGA NAVAREA/HYDROPAC warnings or NOAA sources. Launch timing can change, so confirm against current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and VHF broadcasts.
- SpaceX's contact for this operation is regulatory@spacex.com, or VHF-FM channel 05, 06 or 16.
- This is notice information, not navigational advice.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

finalAnswer:
I found one active marine construction notice inside your box. My search wasn't exhaustive, because I couldn't pull the full official Local Notice to Mariners (LNM) list.

**Active now**
- **Waterborne crane operations, East River Main Channel**
  - Position: 40°42.348'N, 73°58.955'W (about 40.706, -73.983). That's at the southern edge of your box, near the Brooklyn and Manhattan Bridges.
  - Contractor: Grace Industries LLC, supporting building construction, with cranes and material barges on site.
  - Dates and hours: July 20 to December 31, 2026, Monday to Saturday, 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM.
  - Mariner guidance: use slow speed ("slowbell") near the work. Contact the operation on VHF 16, 13 or 61A.
  - Source: a USCG First (Northeast) District LNM, republished by Waterway Guide and dated May 28, 2026.

**Expired or not construction**
- **Marine soil borings:** the liftboat VOYAGER (NorthStar Marine) was doing geotechnical borings between Sutton Place and Roosevelt Island, near the Queensboro Bridge. The notice covered May 1 to June 5, 2026, so it has ended. My source was an East River Keeper post quoting the LNM, not the notice itself.
- **UNGA security zones:** these ran Sept 22 to 28 between E. 36th St and the Queensboro Bridge. They were a security measure, not construction, and have ended.
- **Roosevelt Island tidal energy safety zone:** this dates from 2020 and has expired.
- **Broadway Bridge closure:** this is on the Harlem River, so it is outside your area.
- **Aids to navigation:** East River Regulatory Lights C and E are listed as discrepancies (off station or structure destroyed). That's an aids-to-navigation problem, not a construction notice.

**Unconfirmed:** Donjon Marine posted a barge photo near the Queensboro and Brooklyn Bridges on Oct 8. I found no notice for it, so I can't say whether it's related to a permitted job.

**Coverage gaps**
- I couldn't load the official Northeast District LNM 40/2026 or the NAVCEN (Coast Guard Navigation Center) site, so there may be notices I missed.
- Bridge work and NYC DOT or NYC Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC) pier and ferry-landing projects might also be active in the box but didn't show up.
- Before you rely on any of this, check the current LNM at navcen.uscg.gov/msi and listen to VHF 16.

# NY: East River Main Channel, New York, EAST RIVER, Crane Operations

*   **Date Reported**: May 28, 2026
*   **Reporter**: Waterway Guide Staff
*   **Source**: [USCG District 1](https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi)
*   **Description**:
    
    This Local Notice to Mariners (LNM) report, submitted to the U.S. Coast Guard First District, announces upcoming waterborne crane operations in support of building construction on the **East River**, **New York**. The project, managed by Grace Industries LLC, will take place from **July 20, 2026**, through **December 31, 2026**. Operations are scheduled Monday through Saturday, from **6:00 AM** to **6:00 PM**, with cranes and material barges present at the site.
    
    Mariners in the area are advised to use slow speed ("slowbell") near the crane operations and may contact the operation via marine radio channels 16, 13, and 61A for coordination.
    
      
    
*   **Lat / Lon**: N 40° 42.348' / W 073° 58.955'

\[UPDATE 👉 The VOYAGER is still there, repositioning and crawling across the East River. From the [@uscg](https://www.instagram.com/uscg/)’s Local Notice to Mariners: it’s “Conducting marine soil borings on the East River from May 1st to June 5th, 24 hours a day, seven days a week.” Not to bore you with the Google AI details: “Marine soil borings and geotechnical investigations in riverbeds are conducted to map sub-surface soil conditions, evaluate bearing capacity for heavy structures (bridges, docks), assess risks like scour, liquefaction, and settlement, and check environmental and safety compliance.”\]  
  
Hanging like a spider from a web spun of Queensboro Bridge girders and Roosevelt Island Tram wires, New Jersey-based [@northstar\_marine](https://www.instagram.com/northstar_marine/)’s 145’ [#liftboat](https://www.instagram.com/explore/tags/liftboat/), VOYAGER, sits above the East River between Sutton Place and Roosevelt Island. It arrived on May 4th.  
  
It’s amazing to think those three poles can find a safe and secure footing on the riverbed to withstand the strong 5-6 knot currents of the tidal strait that whips north and south.  
  
According to NorthStar’s website, with a 100’ max water working depth, the “liftboat provides stable, self-elevating platforms for offshore construction, maintenance, and drilling activities. By combining offshore capability with elevated access, they enable safe and efficient operations in challenging environments.” If you’re curious, swipe to the specs and deck plans in the last five photos. The VIP room on the spec sheet caught my interest!  
  
What could it be up to? Enquiring minds wanna know. And if you know, let us know in the comments or reach out to the [@rooseveltislander](https://www.instagram.com/rooseveltislander/), so we’re all in the know, no?

Yes. A check of the Coast Guard's NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information datasets (Local Notice to Mariners geospatial records) found two active marine construction notices within 5 nm of 38.89, -77.05. The datasets were published Oct 7–8, 2026, and all four construction layers were checked.

**1. Tidal Basin and West Potomac Park Seawall Rehabilitation (MSI #270)**
- **Distance:** about 0.16 nm from your point. The notice polygon sits just southeast of it.
- **Waterway:** Potomac River, along West Potomac Park, from Arlington Memorial Bridge to the Inlet Bridge.
- **Effective:** 2024-09-09 to 2027-02-01. The contractor, Cianbro, is working for the National Park Service, and waterside work is due to finish by the end of 2026.
- **Activity:**
  - Temporary trestles, one in the river and one in the Tidal Basin.
  - Turbidity curtains and two turbidity monitoring buoys.
  - Boats, crane barges and material barges.
- **Mariner request:** Stay out of the work area and keep a respectful distance. Minimize wake.

**2. Long Bridge and Pedestrian Bridge construction, Washington Channel (MSI #31521)**
- **Distance:** about 0.97 nm from your point, at 38.882, -77.032.
- **Waterway:** Georgetown Channel / Washington Channel, between the CSX Long Bridge and the I-395 Bridge.
- **Effective:** 2025-11-04 to 2030-01-01. The contractor is North Skanska Flatiron Joint Venture.
- **Activity:**
  - Installing mooring anchors and buoys.
  - Driving 36" steel pile.
  - Building a trestle across the Washington Channel to about 200 ft from the existing bridge.
  - The trestle supports the widening of the CSX Long Bridge rail bridge.

**Limits of this check**
- It did not cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, or records without geometry.
- This is not navigational advice. Check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners (navcen.uscg.gov/msi) and VHF broadcasts before transiting.

I couldn't confirm any current official navigation hazards near 39.47 N, 74.29 W. I found no active warning for that location, but the data I could reach was out of date and incomplete, so don't read that as "all clear."

The position is in the Atlantic Ocean, a few miles off Atlantic City, New Jersey, near the Absecon Inlet approaches. It falls in NAVAREA IV and USCG District 5 (Sector Delaware Bay).

- **NGA NAVAREA IV warnings:** the feed returned data, but the newest message was dated 8 May 2024. That's well behind today's date (about October 2026), so I can't treat it as current. None of its in-force warnings are near your position. The only U.S. coastal entry was the Port of Baltimore restriction at 39°16′N 076°35′W, which is in Chesapeake Bay, far from you.
- **USCG Broadcast Notice to Mariners (District 5):** the search page loaded, but it only shows a search form. The results are loaded by a form I couldn't submit. I couldn't read any Sector Delaware Bay notices, which is where hazards for this area would appear.
- **USCG Local Notice to Mariners (weekly PDF):** I only reached the index page, not the current District 5 PDF.

To check this yourself, use the sources below, which are the authoritative ones for that location:
1. USCG Broadcast Notice to Mariners, District 5, Sector Delaware Bay: https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/broadcast-notice-to-mariners-search?district=5. You can also subscribe there for email or RSS alerts.
2. USCG weekly Local Notice to Mariners, District 5: https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/local-notices-to-mariners-by-cg-district
3. NGA NAVAREA IV warnings: https://msi.nga.mil/NavWarnings
4. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Notices to Navigation Interests, for inlet and channel shoaling: https://ndc.ops.usace.army.mil
5. VHF Channel 16 and the NOAA Weather Radio marine broadcasts. For anything urgent, call USCG Sector Delaware Bay.

Check NOAA's current charts and the U.S. Coast Pilot as well. This summary is not a substitute for them if you're navigating.

Yes. The USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information data, checked on 9 Oct 2026, lists two active hazards to navigation within 5 nm of 38.68 N, 75.10 W. Both are in Rehoboth Bay (Indian River Inlet area), both report shoaling, and both are in Coast Guard District 5.

**Hazards to navigation**
1. **Shoaling at the Rehoboth–Lewes canal entrance (MSI #61), 0.15 nm from your point.**
   - It is centered at 38.68251 N, 75.10012 W.
   - Shoaling runs from the entrance to the Rehoboth–Lewes canal south to Rehoboth Bay Channel Buoy 3 (LLNR 2100), with depths of 2–4 ft at mean low water.
   - It is active from 2024-08-01 to 2027-11-13.
2. **Shoaling in Baker's Channel (MSI #62), about 2.7 nm south.**
   - It lies between Baker's Channel Lighted Buoys 1A and 1B, and between Lighted Buoys 5 and 6. DNREC has marked it with two "DANGER SHOAL" warning buoys.
   - The record shows as active, with an end date of 2029-07-05. The text inside it says "From 2024-08-01 To 2025-08-19", so the dates conflict. Confirm that one with the Coast Guard.

**Other active notices in the area**
- **Dredging (MSI #51875), about 0.4 nm away.**
  - The Dredge Rockbridge is working in the Lewes and Rehoboth Canal from 2026-08-24 to 2027-03-11. The work covers the whole canal, ending at the Lewes and Rehoboth Canal Jetty Warning Light in Rehoboth Bay.
  - Pipelines, anchors, cables and buoys are in the water. Contact the dredge on VHF 13 or 16 before passing.
- **Marine event notice.** A District 5 notice about the new marine event permit process covers a very large area that includes your point. It is administrative and not a physical hazard.

**Limits of this check**
- The Coast Guard's safety-zone line dataset (`safeZoneLine_1`) was not published, so line-type safety zones were not checked. The other safety-zone datasets were checked and returned nothing.
- Broadcast Notices to Mariners, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, bridge notices, and NOAA/NGA sources were not checked.

This is not navigational advice. Check current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and the latest charts before transiting.

There are 2 USCG-reported hazards to navigation in the box 28.5–29.5°N, 92.0–91.0°W. Both are platform-removal buoys in Eugene Island Block 123, and neither is in effect yet.

I checked the USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information hazard layers (point, line and polygon) on 2026-10-09 at about 12:19 UTC. All three layers were checked successfully. Both records are Local Notice to Mariners records from Sector New Orleans (District 8, EEZ).

| # | MSI UID | Location | Effective |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 55334 | 28°56.0′N, 91°21.6′W (Platform A) | 2026-10-10 to 2027-01-01 |
| 2 | 55335 | 28°56.9′N, 91°20.5′W (Platform B) | 2026-10-10 to 2027-01-01 |

- **Type:** Both are listed as Obstructions (Hazards to Navigation).
- **What happened:** Platform removal is under way at Eugene Island Area, Block 123. The topside portions of each platform have been removed, but the subsea portions remain.
- **Marking:** A white and orange buoy with a flashing white light is temporarily established at each platform to mark the subsea hazards. Each buoy stays until site clearance is complete.
- **Guidance:** Mariners are urged to avoid the area.

**Limits of this check:**
- **Not covered:** It does not include Broadcast Notices to Mariners (BNM), NGA NAVAREA warnings, NOAA chart data, or records without geometry. Check those and VHF broadcasts before transiting.
- **Zero matches caveat:** The data says a lack of matches doesn't prove an area is free of hazards.
- **Not for navigation:** This is information only. Use official charts and current notices for actual navigation.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

finalAnswer:
I couldn't pull a live Coast Guard notice feed for this stretch of channel. The sites that carry the live notices (Homeport, and the Local Notice to Mariners and Broadcast Notice to Mariners search results) either failed or returned no notice listings. Below is what I could confirm from the Federal Register, and none of it is a live notice.

**Location:** 29.73, -95.03 is on the upper Houston Ship Channel, near Baytown and Lynchburg. That is under Coast Guard Sector Houston-Galveston (Captain of the Port).

**Rule in effect that is probably relevant (published Dec 29, 2025):**
- **Safety Zone: Beltway 8 Bridge Construction, Houston Ship Channel.**
  - It covers channel waters around the Sam Houston Tollway Ship Channel Bridge, for construction and demolition of the new bridge.
  - It is in effect from Dec 29, 2025 through March 1, 2030.
  - No vessel or person may enter unless the Captain of the Port authorizes it.
  - An earlier version (July 2025) set 120-yard-radius zones at about 29°44.2′N, 95°8.8′W (north shore) and 29°44.1′N, 95°8.8′W (south shore).
  - That is about 7 miles west of your point, so it is upstream of you. It matters if you transit toward Houston.

**Other recent Houston Ship Channel actions (all on the Federal Register):**
- **Gantry-crane transfer safety zones.** Moving zones (about 100 yards) and fixed zones (about 25 yards) have been issued around specific ships, such as the M/V ZHEN HUA 24 (Jan 2026), M/V SUOMIGRACHT (Jan 2026) and M/V SAMPOGRACHT (Dec 2025). Each applies only to that ship's transit and mooring, and these are likely expired. The Federal Register listing (2026-15212) also records a safety zone for the Houston Ship Channel and Seabrook, effective 3/22/2026 (docket USCG-2026-0294).
- **Cruise ship escorts.** Station Galveston ran one near the channel on Aug 20, 2026, a routine security operation.

**Not checked:** Temporary safety zones and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, which can be issued the same day. Also not checked: Army Corps of Engineers dredging notices, and any weather, fog or draft restrictions. These can matter more for day-to-day transit.

**For current notices, use:**
- **Broadcast Notice to Mariners search:** NAVCEN, District 8, Sector 25 Houston-Galveston, at navcen.uscg.gov/broadcast-notice-to-mariners-search?district=8.
- **Weekly Local Notice to Mariners:** NAVCEN's Heartland District (Gulf Coast) edition.
- **Homeport:** the Houston-Galveston port page.
- **Sector Houston-Galveston by VHF:** channel 16, or Vessel Traffic Service Houston-Galveston.

If you're transiting, check those sources directly, because a recent safety zone could be missing from what I found.

finalAnswer:
I couldn't retrieve the area-specific USCG notices for 40.4–40.9 N, 74.3–73.7 W. That box covers New York Harbor, the Raritan Bay approaches and the New Jersey and Long Island coast, which falls under Coast Guard Northeast District (D1) and Sector New York. I only got a few national bulletins and the pointers below.

**What I got**

National Marine Safety Information Bulletins (MSIBs) from NAVCEN, listed as of 9 Oct 2026. They apply everywhere, not just to your area, and none is a hazard or navigation warning for it.

| MSIB | Subject | Date |
|---|---|---|
| 06-26 | Commercial Diving Casualty Reporting (supersedes and cancels MSIB 004-14) | 2026-09-09 |
| 05-26 | Maritime Security Program (MSP) Select Eligibility | 2026-08-26 |
| 04-26 | Applicability of MTSA Cybersecurity Requirements for Inactive Vessels | 2026-08-19 |
| 03-26 | Update to Reporting Sexual Misconduct and Harassment on US Vessels | 2026-08-13 |
| 02-26 | National Recreational Boating Safety Survey | 2026-05-14 |
| 01-26 | Major Ship Arrival Notification System (SANS) Update | 2026-05-01 |

The bulletins are at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msib-national.

**What I couldn't get**

- **Broadcast Notices to Mariners (BNMs):** The search page is an interactive form (district, sector, date range). It returned only the form and no messages. For your area, select District 1 (Northeast), then Sector **New York** (the code is 1,7). You may also want **Long Island Sound** if you work the eastern edge. The page is https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/broadcast-notice-to-mariners-search?district=1.
- **Local Notice to Mariners (LNM), District 1:** The weekly PDF has discrepancies, aids-to-navigation changes, bridge and construction notices, and dredging and other hazards. The D1 download page returned an error, so I couldn't read it. The weekly index is https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/local-notices-to-mariners-by-cg-district.
- **Other USCG sources I didn't reach:** Bridge notices (https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/bridge-notices), Vessel Traffic Services (https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/vessel-traffic-services) and the Sector New York pages on Homeport. I didn't pull these. Sector New York VTS covers much of this box.

**To get notices for this area**

- Subscribe to BNM and LNM email or RSS for Sector New York at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/subscribe-email-rss-feeds.
- For live information, listen to VHF-FM Ch. 16 and the scheduled Sector New York broadcasts, or call the Sector command center.
- Check the NGA Notice to Mariners (https://msi.nga.mil/NGAPortal/MSI.portal) and USACE Notices to Navigation Interests (https://ndc.ops.usace.army.mil), which also cover shoaling and dredging in the channels.

Don't use this for navigation. I can try again with a different route if you'd like, or pull the NOAA marine forecast for the area, though that isn't a USCG product.

finalAnswer:
I found no current U.S. Coast Guard notice that sits on your track. I couldn't read the official sources directly, though, so treat this as a partial check.

Your track runs from about Victoria to just southeast of Cape Flattery. It's the length of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, crossing the U.S./Canada line.

**U.S. Coast Guard notices for this area**
These come from Northwest District (D13) Local Notice to Mariners 40/2026, issued 7 Oct 2026. I read them through a mirror of the notices, SeaLagom, not through the Coast Guard's own NAVCEN site.
- **Sequim Bay, about 48-04N 123-01W:** two Pacific Northwest National Laboratory notices (LNM13-580644 and LNM13-86A564).
  - One covers an autonomous docking platform and an autonomous surface vessel. They will be deployed about 10 days in total between 21 Sep and 21 Dec 2026, in daylight only, and may be left unattended for up to 2 hours.
  - The other covers a research buoy at about 48-04.7N 123-01.9W, in place for about 6 months.
  - Both ask you to use caution and reduce wake. The research vessel can be hailed on VHF 16.
  - Sequim Bay is inshore of your track. It matters only if you pass or stop near Sequim.
- **Admiralty Inlet regatta (LNM13-490ACD):** this is in Puget Sound, not on your route, and it was archived on 7 Oct.
- **NASA Crew-12 reentry hazard areas (NAVAREA XII):** these run from 6 Oct to 19 Oct 2026, with three overlapping areas. They lie offshore, between about 37°N and 45.5°N and well west of the coast. Your track at about 48.3–48.4°N is north of them. Check them if you plan to continue offshore or south.
- Everything else I saw was in the Columbia River, Oregon coast, Puget Sound, Hood Canal and similar areas, so it doesn't apply to your route.

**What I couldn't check**
- I only read page 1 of 2 of the D13 list, which showed the most recent notices. Page 2 may have older notices that are still in force.
- The NAVCEN LNM page loaded with no notice content, so I couldn't confirm these against the Coast Guard's own listing.
- I didn't get any Canadian Coast Guard NAVWARNs or Notices to Mariners (NOTMAR). Your first leg is in Canadian waters, and the Canadian portal returned only a landing page.
- I didn't pull the NGA Broadcast Warnings.

**Before you go, check these directly**
1. USCG NAVCEN, D13 Local Notice to Mariners (navcen.uscg.gov).
2. Canadian NAVWARNs for the Pacific region at nis.ccg-gcc.gc.ca, and NOTMAR at notmar.gc.ca.
3. NGA broadcast warnings for NAVAREA XII at msi.nga.mil.
4. Marine weather and any gale or small craft advisories for the Strait. These are NWS/ECCC products, not Coast Guard notices.
5. Vessel traffic: the Strait has a traffic separation scheme, and the U.S. and Canada run a cooperative vessel traffic service (Seattle Traffic and Tofino/Victoria MCTS). Also check for naval or range activity near Cape Flattery.

If you give me your departure date and vessel type, I can look through page 2 and try the Canadian and NGA sources again.

# Navigational Warnings and Notices

Current navigational warnings (NAVWARNs), including notices to shipping, notices to mariners (NOTMAR), shoals and status of aids to navigation.

## Most requested

*   [Interactive Map](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/interactive-map)
*   [Tides, Water Levels and Currents](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/water-levels/index-en)
*   [Marine Weather](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/meteo/index-en)
*   [Nautical Charts](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/charts/index-en)
*   [Ice breaking and Ice Conditions](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/ice/index-en)
*   [Search and Rescue](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/sar/index-en)
*   [Aids to Navigation](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/aids/index-en)

## National services and information

### [Navigational Warnings (NAVWARNs)](https://nis.ccg-gcc.gc.ca/public/rest/menu/en/topics)

NAVWARNs contain information about changes to navigational aids and current marine activities or hazards. Visit [Navigational and NAVAREA warnings](https://www.canada.ca/en/canadian-coast-guard/services/marine-communications-traffic-services/navigational-navarea-warnings.html) for more information.

### [Notices to Mariners (NOTMAR)](https://www.notmar.gc.ca/index-en.php)

Provides the necessary information to update charts and nautical publications.

### [US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (for US Waters)](https://msi.nga.mil/)

Provides warnings and notices for geographical sea regions known as NAVAREAs, including NAVAREA XII.

*   [Notices to Mariners (US)](https://msi.nga.mil/NTM)
    
*   [Broadcast Warnings (US)](https://msi.nga.mil/NavWarnings)
    
*   [NAVAREA XII Broadcast Warnings (US)](https://msi.nga.mil/queryResults?publications/broadcast-warn?navArea=12&status=active&output=html)
    

### [US Coast Guard Navigation Center (for US Waters)](http://www.navcen.uscg.gov/?pageName=lnmMain)

Enhance the safety, security, and efficiency of U.S. Waterways; enable effective Coast Guard operations, and maximize the utility of GPS for its civil users.

*   [Great Lakes (US)](http://www.navcen.uscg.gov/?pageName=lnmDistrict&region=9)
    

## Regional services and information

### [NAVAREA Broadcast Warning Messages](https://nis.ccg-gcc.gc.ca/public/rest/messages/en/search-navareas)

Arctic region

Canadian Coast Guard is responsible for Broadcast Warning Messages in [NAVAREA XVII](https://nis.ccg-gcc.gc.ca/public/rest/messages/en/search-navareas?q=&status=PUBLISHED&from=&to=&navareas=2&sortBy=DATE&maxHits=20) and [NAVAREA XVIII](https://nis.ccg-gcc.gc.ca/public/rest/messages/en/search-navareas?q=&status=PUBLISHED&from=&to=&navareas=4&sortBy=DATE&maxHits=20).

### [Avadepth](https://www2.pac.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/index-eng.html)

Pacific region

Forecasts of available water depths for vessels navigating the Fraser River South Arm Channel

### [Shoals in the Waterways](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/notices/central/shoals/index-en)

Central region

St. Lawrence River, St. Mary's River, St. Clair River and Detroit River.

*   [Download in Force Shoals](https://e-navigation.canada.ca/topics/notices/central/shoals/download)
    

### [Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway System](https://greatlakes-seaway.com/en/news-and-information/notices/)

Central region

Seaway Notices address issues specific to a given navigation season, and serve to complement the regulations found in the Seaway Handbook.

**Port Canaveral nearshore marine forecast (0–20 nm)**
Source: NWS Melbourne, zone AMZ552, issued 2:24 AM EDT Fri Oct 9, 2026.

**Saturday**
- Winds: south, around 15 knots
- Seas: 3–4 ft, with east swell of 3 ft at 6 seconds
- Water surface: moderate chop on the intracoastal waters
- Weather: chance of thunderstorms. Chance of showers in the morning, then showers likely in the afternoon.

**Saturday night**
- Winds: south, 10–15 knots
- Seas: 3–4 ft, with east swell of 3 ft at 6 seconds
- Water surface: light chop
- Weather: showers likely with a chance of thunderstorms in the evening. After midnight, a chance of showers and a slight chance of thunderstorms.

**Sunday**
- Winds: south, 5–10 knots
- Seas: 2–3 ft, with east swell of 3 ft at 7 seconds
- Water surface: light chop
- Weather: morning has a chance of showers and a slight chance of thunderstorms. Afternoon has showers likely and a chance of thunderstorms.

**Sunday night**
- Winds: south around 5 knots, becoming west after midnight
- Seas: 2–3 ft
- Water surface: mostly smooth
- Weather: slight chance of showers and thunderstorms.

**Summary**
- Saturday is the choppier day, with 15-knot southerly winds and 3–4 ft seas, and showers building through the afternoon and evening.
- Sunday is calmer, with lighter winds and 2–3 ft seas. Showers and thunderstorms are still likely in the afternoon.
- Both days carry thunderstorm risk. Winds and seas will be higher in and near any storms. The best window for being on the water is Saturday morning or Sunday morning.
- Conditions improve Monday, with northwest winds of 5–10 knots and 2–3 ft seas.

This is a forecast from this morning, so it can change. Check the NWS Melbourne marine forecast, or a NOAA VHF weather broadcast, before you head out. This is also general guidance, not a go/no-go decision for any particular vessel.

Unsourced material may be challenged and [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Burden_of_evidence "Wikipedia:Verifiability").  
_Find sources:_ ["Workweek and weekend"](https://www.google.com/search?as_eq=wikipedia&q=%22Workweek+and+weekend%22) – [news](https://www.google.com/search?tbm=nws&q=%22Workweek+and+weekend%22+-wikipedia&tbs=ar:1) **·** [newspapers](https://www.google.com/search?&q=%22Workweek+and+weekend%22&tbs=bkt:s&tbm=bks) **·** [books](https://www.google.com/search?tbs=bks:1&q=%22Workweek+and+weekend%22+-wikipedia) **·** [scholar](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Workweek+and+weekend%22) **·** [JSTOR](https://www.jstor.org/action/doBasicSearch?Query=%22Workweek+and+weekend%22&acc=on&wc=on) _(January 2014)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance_template_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

 The **weekdays** and **weekend** are the complementary parts of the [week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Week "Week"), devoted to [labour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_\(economics\) "Labour (economics)") and [rest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leisure "Leisure"), respectively. The legal **weekdays** ([British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English "British English")), or **workweek** ([American English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English "American English")), is the part of the seven-day week devoted to working. In most of the world, the workweek is from [Monday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday "Monday") to [Friday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friday "Friday") and the weekend is [Saturday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday "Saturday") and [Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday "Sunday"). A **weekday** or **workday** is any day of the working week. Other institutions often follow this pattern, such as places of [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education "Education"). The constituted weekend has varying definitions, based on determined calendar days, designated period of time, and/or regional definition of the working week (e.g., commencing after 5:00 p.m. on Friday and lasting until 6:00 p.m. on Sunday). Sometimes the term "weekend" is expanded to include the time after work hours on the last workday of the week. Weekdays and workdays can be further detailed in terms of [working time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_time "Working time"), the period of time that an individual spends at paid occupational labor.

In many Christian traditions, Sunday is the "[day of rest and worship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Day "Lord's Day")". The [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism") _[Shabbat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabbat "Shabbat")_ or [Biblical Sabbath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biblical_Sabbath_\(Hebrew\) "Biblical Sabbath (Hebrew)") lasts from sunset on Friday to the fall of full darkness on Saturday; as a result, the weekend in Israel is observed on Friday to Saturday. Some Muslim-majority countries historically instituted a Thursday–Friday weekend. Today, many of these countries, in the interests of furthering business trade and cooperation, have shifted to Friday–Saturday or Saturday–Sunday.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-2)

The [Christian day of worship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Day "Lord's Day") is just one day each week, but the preceding day (the Jewish Sabbath) came to be taken as a [holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holiday "Holiday") as well in the 20th century. This shift has been accompanied by a reduction in the total number of hours worked per week. The present-day concept of the "weekend" first arose in the industrial north of Britain in the early 19th century.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-etymonline.com-3) A **day off** is a non-working day, not necessarily on weekends.

Some countries have adopted a six-day workweek and one-day weekend (6×1), which can be Friday only (in [Djibouti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djibouti "Djibouti"), [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), [Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia "Somalia") and [Libya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya "Libya")), Saturday only (in [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal "Nepal")), or Sunday only (in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"), [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia"), [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda"), [Eritrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrea "Eritrea"), [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"), and [Equatorial Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equatorial_Guinea "Equatorial Guinea")). However, most countries have adopted a five-day workweek and two-day weekend (5×2), whose days differ according to religious tradition: Friday and Saturday (in 17 Muslim countries and [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel")); Saturday and Sunday (most of the countries); or Friday and Sunday (in [Brunei Darussalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunei "Brunei"); [Aceh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aceh "Aceh"), Indonesia; and [Sarawak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarawak "Sarawak"), Malaysia), with the previous evening post-work often considered part of the weekend. Proposals continue to be put forward to reduce the number of days or hours worked per week, such as the [four-day workweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four-day_workweek "Four-day workweek"), on the basis of predicted social and economic benefits.

## History

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Workweek_and_weekend&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")\]

See also: [Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Week "Week")

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Workweeks-map.svg/500px-Workweeks-map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Workweeks-map.svg)

World map showing the days of the work week by country:

  Monday – Friday

  Monday – Saturday

  Sunday – Thursday

  Sunday – Friday

  Saturday – Thursday

  Monday – Thursday and Saturday

  Mixed

A continuous seven-day cycle that runs throughout history, paying no attention whatsoever to the phases of the moon and having a fixed day of rest, was most likely first practised in [Judaism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism"), dated to the 6th century BC at the latest.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-5)

In [Ancient Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") (753 BC–476 AD), every eight days there was a [nundinae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nundinae "Nundinae"). It was a market day, during which children were exempted from school[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-6) and agricultural workers stopped work in the field and came to the city to sell the produce of their labor[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-8) or to practice religious rites.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

The [French Revolutionary Calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolutionary_Calendar "French Revolutionary Calendar") (1793–1805) had ten-day weeks (called _décades_) and allowed _décadi_, one out of the 10 days, as a leisure day. From 1929 to 1940, the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") utilized [a calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_calendar "Soviet calendar") with five and six-day work weeks, with a rest day assigned to a worker either with a colour or number.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

During the [Han dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Han_dynasty "Han dynasty") of imperial [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), officials had a day off once every five days known as _hsui-mu_ （休沐）.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-:0-9) This rest day was known as "a day for rest and for washing one's hair".[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-:0-9)

In cultures with a [four-day workweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four-day_workweek "Four-day workweek"), the three [Sabbaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabbath "Sabbath") derive from the culture's main religious tradition: Friday ([Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Sabbath "Muslim Sabbath")), Saturday ([Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_Sabbath "Jewish Sabbath")), and Sunday ([Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Sabbath "Christian Sabbath")).[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-10)

The present-day concept of the relatively longer "week-end" first arose in the industrial north of Britain in the early 19th century[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-etymonline.com-3) and was originally a voluntary arrangement between factory owners and workers allowing Saturday afternoon off starting at two pm on the basis that staff would be available for work sober and refreshed on Monday morning.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-ReferenceA-11) The _[Oxford English Dictionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_English_Dictionary "Oxford English Dictionary")_ traces the first use of the term "weekend" to the British magazine _[Notes and Queries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notes_and_Queries "Notes and Queries")_ in 1879.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-12)

In 1884, the Federation of Organized Trades and Labor Unions, a predecessor of the [AFL-CIO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFL-CIO "AFL-CIO") created mid-twentieth century, called for all workers to have eight-hour days by May 1, 1886, playing a crucial role in the push for a five-day workweek.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-13) In 1908, the first five-day workweek in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") was instituted by a [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England") [cotton mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill") so that [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish "Jewish") workers would not have to work on the Sabbath from sundown Friday to sundown Saturday.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-theatlantic.com-14) In 1926, [Henry Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Ford "Henry Ford") began shutting down his [automotive factories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_factory "Car factory") for all of Saturday and Sunday, realizing that by giving workers more time off it would encourage more leisure activities such as vacations and shopping.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-15) In 1929, the [Amalgamated Clothing Workers of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amalgamated_Clothing_Workers_of_America "Amalgamated Clothing Workers of America") was the first union to demand and receive a five-day workweek. The rest of the United States slowly followed, but it was not until 1940, when a provision of the 1938 [Fair Labor Standards Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Labor_Standards_Act_of_1938 "Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938") mandating a maximum 40-hour workweek went into effect, that the two-day weekend was adopted nationwide.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-theatlantic.com-14)

Over the succeeding decades, particularly in the 1940s to 1960s, an increasing number of countries adopted either a Friday–Saturday or a Saturday–Sunday weekend to harmonize with international markets. A series of workweek reforms in the mid-to-late 2000s and early 2010s brought much of the [Arab world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world "Arab world") in synchronization with the majority of countries around the world, in terms of working hours, the length of the workweek, and the days of the weekend. The [International Labour Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Labour_Organization "International Labour Organization") (ILO) currently defines a workweek exceeding 48 hours as excessive. A 2007 study by the ILO found that at least 614.2 million people around the world were working excessive hours.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-16)

## Length

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Workweek_and_weekend&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Length")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Almost_empty_calendar.JPG/250px-Almost_empty_calendar.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Almost_empty_calendar.JPG)

This day planner chart (which can be used for any months) shows the workweek days as white boxes and the weekend days as light blue-coloured boxes.

Actual workweek lengths have been falling in the developed world. In the United States, the workweek length decreased slowly from before [the Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War") to the start of the 20th century. There was a rapid reduction between 1900 and 1920, especially between 1913 and 1919, when weekly hours fell by about eight percent.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-hunnicutt-17) In 1926, [Henry Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Ford "Henry Ford") standardized on a five-day workweek, instead of the prevalent six days, without reducing employees' pay.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-lombardo-18) Hours worked stabilized at about 49 per week during the 1920s, and during the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") fell below 40.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-hunnicutt-17) During the Depression, President [Herbert Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Hoover "Herbert Hoover") called for a reduction in work hours in lieu of layoffs. Later, President [Franklin Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_Roosevelt "Franklin Roosevelt") signed the [Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Labor_Standards_Act_of_1938 "Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938"), which established a five-day, 40-hour workweek for many workers.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-lombardo-18) The proportion of people working very long weeks has since risen, and the full-time employment of women has increased dramatically.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-rones-19)

The [New Economics Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Economics_Foundation "New Economics Foundation") has recommended moving to a 21-hour standard workweek to address problems with unemployment, high carbon emissions, low well-being, entrenched inequalities, [overworking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overwork "Overwork"), family care, and the general lack of free time.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-lombardo-18)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-nef21-20)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Workweek_and_weekend#cite_note-guardian-21)[\[22\]](https:

finalAnswer:
The EVER GIVEN is off the coast of **South Africa**, heading for Singapore. VesselFinder's AIS data had the position as about 6 hours old when I checked.

- **Vessel:** EVER GIVEN, a container ship (IMO 9811000, MMSI 636026627) flagged in Liberia.
- **Status:** Under way, at about 18.1 knots.
- **Destination:** Singapore, with an ETA of Oct 23, 17:00.
- **Last port:** Hamburg, Germany. It left on Sep 23 at 19:02 UTC.
- **Draught:** 11.5 m.

The page gave only "South Africa" as the location, not exact coordinates. The exact live position is on VesselFinder's map: https://www.vesselfinder.com/?imo=9811000. VesselFinder also mentioned a satellite position from 2 minutes ago, but that's behind a paid plan.

The MyShipTracking and MarineTraffic pages I pulled were map apps that didn't load any position data, so I'm relying on VesselFinder alone.

- **Source:** NOAA NCEI's bathymetric elevation model returned −18.26 m at 40.69, −74.03. The point is in Upper New York Bay, just east of Liberty Island.

- **Chart query:** I also queried NOAA's electronic navigational chart service for the exact point. It returned no features.

This area is dredged and near the shipping channels. Actual depths change quickly over short distances, so don't use this for navigation. For that, check the current NOAA chart (12327 or 12334) or the latest ENC in a chart viewer. The NOAA Chart Locator or Chart Viewer will show the official soundings.

prompt: Plan the fastest sailing route from Miami to Nassau.
finalAnswer:
# Miami to Nassau: fastest sailing route

I haven't pulled live weather or charts, so this is a planning outline. Check current conditions before you commit.

## Route options

| Route | Approx. distance | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Direct via Bimini and the Great Bahama Bank** | about 185–200 nm | Fastest for shallow-draft boats (under about 5 ft). It means crossing the Gulf Stream, then the Bank, then Northwest Channel. |
| **B. Deep-water route via the Northwest Providence Channel** | about 190–200 nm | Fastest for deeper-draft boats (over about 5–6 ft). It stays in deep water, with no shoals and no daylight-only restrictions. |

Both routes take roughly **24–32 hours** at 6–8 knots.

## Waypoints

1. **Depart Miami at Government Cut (Fisher Island) in the afternoon.**
2. **Head east-southeast, about 090–100°T, across the Gulf Stream.**
   - The Stream sets north at 2–3 knots. Aim south of your target and steer an upstream-biased course, or you'll be pushed north.
   - Don't plan on a straight rhumb line. Plot a course through the water that cancels the set.
3. **Route A:**
   - Go south of Bimini, through Gun Cay Cut or Cat Cay.
   - Cross the Bank to Northwest Channel Light.
   - Continue east-northeast to Nassau Harbour, entering from the north.
   - Do the Bank crossing in daylight if you can.
4. **Route B:**
   - Go north of Bimini, then east through the Northwest Providence Channel.
   - Pass north of the Berry Islands.
   - Turn south to Nassau Harbour from the northwest.
5. **Clear customs at Nassau.** Fly the Q flag on arrival.

## Tips for the fastest passage

- **Wait for a southeast to south wind.** It gives you a beam or broad reach.
- **Avoid any northerly component.** North wind against the Gulf Stream builds steep, dangerous seas. Cold fronts are the main risk, especially in winter.
- **Leave Miami late afternoon.** You cross the Stream in the dark but reach the Bank in the morning light, so you arrive in Nassau the next day.
- **Sail a close-hauled course to the east if the wind is east or southeast.** You may need to motor-sail to hold your time.
- **Check the following before you go:**
  - NOAA marine forecast and the Gulf Stream position (Gulf Stream charts or a service like Windy)
  - Your draft against the Bank depths, since Route A is shoal
  - Fuel for motoring through calms

Tell me your boat type, draft, and cruising speed, and I can refine the route and timing. I can also pull current weather and wind forecasts for the route.

Red snapper rules in federal waters off Florida depend on the coast and on whether you fish from a private boat or a charter. The details below come from the FWC and NOAA Fisheries pages as of early October 2026. Seasons change every year, so check them before you go.

## Gulf coast (Gulf of America)
This applies to private recreational anglers in both state and federal waters. Florida's Gulf state waters run from shore to 9 miles.

- **Minimum size:** 16" total length.
- **Bag limit:** 2 per person per day. Red snapper count toward the 10-fish state snapper aggregate. A charter captain and crew can keep zero.
- **2026 private-vessel season:**
  - Summer: May 22 – July 31, daily.
  - Fall: Sept 1 – Oct 4, daily, and Oct 9 – 22, daily.
  - After that, it's open on set weekends and holidays:
    - Oct 23–25 and Oct 30 – Nov 1 (Fri–Sun)
    - Nov 7–8, 14–15 and 21–22 (Sat–Sun)
    - Nov 26–29 (Thanksgiving weekend)
    - Dec 5–6, 12–13 and 19–20 (Sat–Sun)
    - Dec 25–27 (Christmas weekend)
    - Jan 1–4, 2027, daily
- **Charter boats:** Charter vessels without a federal permit can only harvest in Florida Gulf state waters during this season. Federally permitted for-hire vessels follow a separate federal season that I didn't retrieve, so check with NOAA Fisheries.
- **Gear:** Reef fish gear rules apply.

## Atlantic coast
- **Minimum size:** None.
- **Bag limit:** 1 per person per day, within the 10-fish snapper-grouper aggregate. A charter or headboat captain and crew can keep zero.
- **Season:** The federal season is replaced this year by state-managed seasons under an exempted fishing permit that NOAA issued to Florida. In federal waters the season is:
  - May 22 – June 20
  - Oct 2–4
  - Oct 9–11
  - Oct 16–18

  The FWC page also lists an Atlantic season of Oct 9–22 and doesn't mention the Oct 2–4 and Oct 16–18 dates. The two sources don't fully agree, so confirm the exact dates with FWC.
- **Declaring trips:** Private anglers and for-hire captains must declare all fishing trips, for all fishing days, to take part.
- **Eligibility:** You need the required state licenses and federal permits. Each trip must start and end at a Florida landing location.
- **Gear:** Reef fish gear rules apply.

## Before you go
- The FWC snapper page is https://myfwc.com/fishing/saltwater/recreational/snappers/.
- The Atlantic red snapper page is https://myfwc.com/fishing/saltwater/recreational/atlantic-red-snapper/.
- You can sign up for the State Reef Fish Survey, which FWC recommends for snapper anglers.
- NOAA text alerts for in-season changes: text GULFRECFISH or SATLRECFISH to 888777.

I only covered recreational rules. Commercial seasons and limits are different. Tell me if you want those, or the federal for-hire Gulf season.

# Snappers

## The 2026 Recreational Atlantic Red Snapper Season will be October 9-22

This season will be in Atlantic state and federal waters for private anglers and for-hire captains. Private anglers and for-hire charter captains need to DECLARE all fishing trips for all fishing days to participate!

[Learn More](https://myfwc.com/fishing/saltwater/recreational/atlantic-red-snapper/)

## 2026 Florida Gulf Private Recreational Red Snapper Fall Season is Open

The 2026 Gulf private recreational red snapper fall season is underway. Harvest is open daily from Sept. 1 – October 4 and October 9–22. The season will then continue on scheduled weekends and holidays throughout the year. Please see the complete updated schedule below.

## NEW Recreational Regulations for Gulf Lane Snapper - Effective April 1

The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission approved a new 10 inch minimum size limit and 20 fish bag limit for Gulf lane snapper in Gulf state waters. These new regulations go into effect April 1, 2026.

[Learn More](https://myfwc.com/news/all-news/lane-snapper-1125/)

## Fishing for snappers?

Make sure you're signed up for the State Reef Fish Survey

[Learn more](https://myfwc.com/fishing/saltwater/recreational/state-reef-fish-survey/)

## Gulf Red Snapper

Red snapper are long-lived, early-maturing reef fish that are broadly distributed in the Gulf of America. They can live to be 57. Older, larger females contribute far more eggs than younger, smaller females. To have a sustainable red snapper stock, there should be an abundance of older/larger fish to maximize the number of young fish coming into the fishery.

One 24-inch female red snapper (about an 8 year old fish) produces as many eggs as 212 17-inch females (about 5 years old).
